answer: Echo-Locality Routing. Each agent routes work only to peers whose transaction history overlaps its own across at least three independent channels; a new node must wander between clusters until that overlap accumulates. The graph therefore forms a karst of isolated chambers—sybils cluster together and see only each other's traffic. Attacking requires sustaining genuine diverse interactions per fake identity, and any willow of coordinated nodes is pruned when its internal-only flow is detected. Cost: months of real counterparty work per identity.
